preconditions.expression: all(2 <= int(n) <= 500 and 0 <= int(m) <= int(n) * (int(n) - 1) // 2 for n, m in [line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[0:1]])
preconditions.description: Input must contain exactly one line with integers n (2 ≤ n ≤ 500) and m (0 ≤ m ≤ n·(n−1)/2), representing the number of cities and roads, respectively.

preconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == 3 and all(int(x) >= 1 and int(x) <= int(n) for x in line.split()[:2]) and int(line.split()[2]) >= 1 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:1+m])
preconditions.description: Each of the m following lines must contain three integers xi, yi, li (1 ≤ xi, yi ≤ n, xi ≠ yi, 1 ≤ li ≤ 10^6), representing a bidirectional road between cities xi and yi with length li.

preconditions.expression: all(xi != yi for xi, yi, li in [tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:1+m]])
preconditions.description: No road connects a city to itself (xi ≠ yi).
Input consists of exactly n + m lines: one for n and m, followed by m road descriptions.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == ' '.join(str(cst) for s in range(1, int(n)) for t in range(s+1, int(n)+1) if (cst := count_roads_on_shortest_paths(s, t, parsed_roads, int(n))) is not None else '0')
postconditions.description: For every pair of cities s < t, cst is the number of roads that lie on at least one shortest path from s to t. If no path exists between s and t, cst = 0. The output is a space-separated sequence of cst values for all s < t in lexicographical order.

postconditions.expression: all(cst >= 0 for cst in map(int, stdout.strip().split()))
postconditions.description: Each cst value in the output is a non-negative integer.
The output contains exactly n·(n−1)/2 integers, one for each pair s < t.
